text: In particular, when we look at the first technique that you see here, coding, to introduce redundant bits that help the receiver to understand what would be the correct bits to extract. And these codes are called forward error correction codes, and this is what we are looking at. First, let's focus on on the main message here. Let me show you this figure. So let's consider that we have a certain number of information bits, right? These information bits are divided into blocks. Each block includes n bits, and within each bits, actually, we use key information bits that are user bits, important bits that we really want to transfer. The remaining ones will be bits that are artificially added, so they are redundant bits, and that what we transmit is one block of n bits, one after the other. The receiver will have to extract from each block of n bits the key user bits correct, okay? That's the goal, and we'll use these redundant bits that we artificially inserted.
